 Live Blog: Singapore Airlines unveils next-generation seats and cabin experience
 Aaron Wong 
 Nov 6, 2026 
 7 
 Singapore Airlines finally unveils its next-generation First, Business, Premium Economy and Economy seats today. Join me for live coverage of all the action as it happens.
 Facebook X Telegram WhatsApp 
 📣Key Developments so Far 
 Singapore Airlines is unveiling its next-generation cabin products and new travel experience at Marina Bay Sands today 
 Event commences at 1.15 p.m 
 Media embargo lifts at 1.30 p.m 
 Hands-on time with new seats this afternoon 
 Join the conversation via this Google Form , or on Telegram 
 Submit your questions about the new seats or cabin experience here 
 Refresh this page for the latest updates. Latest news appears at the top of the page. 
 12.25 p.m
 Now on-site at Marina Bay Sands! Doors open at 12.45 p.m.
 11.48 a.m
 On that note, I’m out the door for a quick lunch, and then off to Marina Bay Sands. I’ll take a brief pause here, and come back around 12.30 p.m or so.
 IT’S HAPPENING. 
 11.45 a.m
 Which route will get the new products first?
 Another big question on everyone’s minds this morning: which route will get the new products first? 
 It’s not clear whether SIA will answer this question today, or keep that up its sleeve until the first retrofitted aircraft is ready to emerge from the hangar, but history shows there are two clear frontrunners.

 *✈️ A very special inaugural flight 
 Singapore Airlines had a special plan to mark the launch of its new B747-400 cabin products in 1998. Instead of flying to one destination, the airline did a round-the-world flight from Singapore – London- Frankfurt – New York- Osaka- Singapore! 
 This aircraft entered into regular service on the Singapore-Frankfurt-New York JFK route later that month. 
 If we ignore the regional Business Class products, then  London (Heathrow, obviously) and Sydney are favourites. These are its flagship, cash cow routes where the airline is fond of showing off its latest and greatest.
 Of the two, Sydney would allow for better product consistency, as the rotation can be handled by a single aircraft (barring any mechanical snafus), enabling SIA to offer the product on a daily basis.
 London is much further away, and the following day’s flight from Singapore would depart before the aircraft from the previous day had a chance to return. Therefore, if London were to be the launch route, then daily service would not be possible until more retrofitted aircraft arrive.
 But it’s not outside the realm of possibility though, because this is precisely what happened back in September 2013. SIA launched its 2013 First and Business Class seats on the B777-300ER to London as a 3x weekly service, before ramping up to daily service when more aircraft became available (incidentally, the new aircraft also served Tokyo Narita occasionally during this period).
 I’m more fuzzy about whether SIA will do live crew familiarisation for the new product, or stick with ground-based training. If so, we might even see the first retrofitted aircraft flying to places like Bangkok, Jakarta and Kuala Lumpur before it goes on long-haul duty. 
 11.43 a.m
 DoA (dated on arrival?)
 Of course, there are concerns. The designs were signed off in late 2021, but they’re only making their debut more than five years later (remember, Q1 2027 is the projected entry-into-service date).
 Will the seats be dated on arrival? Did SIA make any substantial changes during COVID?  And how much can you really change to a seat without having to get it certified all over again?
 11.40 a.m
 Further surprises today?
 Cabin products aside, could SIA still spring some surprises on us today? 
 Well, there are two big things I’m wondering about. 
 First, caviar in Business Class . Back in August 2025, I flagged that Singapore Airlines had launched a tender for Business Class caviar. While the idea would have been outlandish a decade ago, caviar has been slowly filtering down to the unwashed masses in Business Class. 
 Qatar Airways got the ball rolling in August 2024, when it started serving Business Class passengers  on selected routes a 15-gram portion of Baerii caviar, paired with Balik salmon (dubbed “the best smoked salmon in the world”), melba toast, crème fraiche, chives, egg yolks and whites, minced onion and lemon. A mother-of-pearl spoon is provided, of course. 
 Qatar Airways Business Class caviar service | Photo: Qatar Airways 
 THAI Airways then introduced caviar in Business Class from January 2025, on flights between Bangkok to Europe. While an individual 10-gram tin is provided, this isn’t a full caviar service. Rather, it’s paired with appetisers such as tuna and avocado tartare, or foie gras laab.
 THAI Airways Business Class caviar service | Photo: THAI 
 Even United is offering caviar in Business Class, in a way. Passengers in the eight Polaris Studio seats (the airline’s “Business Plus” product) receive Ossetra caviar, a post-dessert specialty snack box, exclusive entrée options and Laurent-Perrier Cuvee Rose champagne.
 Caviar for Polaris Studio | Photo: United Airlines 
 The second is a possible new bedding partner for First and Business Class — especially the latter. I’d love to see SIA add a mattress pad, because that’s one thing it’s really lacking right now. 
 11.35 a.m
 Your say: SIA vs competitors
 With all the delays to the new cabin products, how would you rate SIA against its competition now? 
 “SQ lags behind in 3 main areas: Starlink, 4K screens, USB-C. In Business, the gap is even bigger in terms of privacy, the awkward flip bed, and an older design vs Qsuites, Aria and the new Polaris” , says Avery, typing from the toilet. You and me both, brother.
 “SIA have been riding on their impeccable service for a tad too long now. Making up for their dated hard products. It’s about time they catch up “, says Jon.
 “ SIA is still firmly in the top three, but Cathay and Qatar are making a strong case for being ahead,” says JD.
 “Instead of setting the yardstick, SIA is now trying to play catch-up in the hard product space – particular in JCL, against the likes of QSuites; The Room; Aria Suites”  says Jo, a mere 20km away from today’s epicentre.
 “SIA may have been late, but being late isn’t the same as being beaten. The airline still sets the standard in service and operational excellence. The question now isn’t whether SIA has caught up—it’s whether today’s launch gives competitors something new to chase. That’s the difference between following the market and leading it.” , says Kelvin.
 11.32 a.m
 No love for Premium Economy and Economy?
 So…that decision to leave Premium Economy and Economy Class out of the A350 refits. That’s something which passengers will be feeling for a very, very long time.
 Sure, there will be new seats on the B777-9, but the timeline on that aircraft is still uncertain. Besides, the A350s are the backbone of the long-haul fleet, which means that passengers in these cabins will be flying into the 2030s and beyond with USB-A ports and 3.5mm audio jacks.
 It’s just very hard news to swallow from an airline that positions itself as World Class.
 💬 Have Your Say 
 What do you make of SIA’s decision to not install new Economy and Premium Economy seats on the A350? 
 ➡️Share your thoughts! 
 11.28 a.m
 What we know about the new Premium Economy and Economy Class
 Over in Premium Economy and Economy, the talk is more about what we won’t see, rather than what we will. 
 On the retrofitted A350s, SIA has confirmed that these two cabins will just be “refreshed”, which means an updated KrisWorld system and new upholstery. That’s it. No 4K screens, no Bluetooth, and no USB-C ports. 
 Singapore Airlines A350 retrofit: Why no love for Premium Economy & Economy? 
 I don’t know what to tell you. I’m just as surprised as you that SIA passengers in these cabins will be flying into the late 2030s with USB-A charging. The existing Economy Class seats on the A350-900LH date back to 2017 (13 of 34 aircraft) or 2013 (21 of 34 aircraft), and I struggle to see how they can last another decade or more. I mean, it’s always possible that SIA plans a separate refresh of these seats, but until we hear otherwise, we have to assume that this is it.
 2013 Economy Class seat | Photo: yflyer on SQTalk 2017 Economy Class seat | Photo: yflyer on SQTalk 
 Mind you, it’s not just the A350. Across the rest of the SIA fleet, these features are nowhere to be found. That’s a pretty damning scorecard, with rivals like STARLUX , Japan Airlines , United Airlines, and Air New Zealand already offering these technological bells and whistles.

 Premium Economy and Economy Class passengers will need to wait until the long-delayed B777-9 arrives — and who knows when that will be?
 Very little has been shown of Premium Economy Class, though we can spy manual seat controls in the video, which means these will not be electrically-powered seats.
 Singapore Airlines new Premium Economy Class seat 
 We also know that Premium Economy will offer up to 16-inch 4K screens, with OLED on selected B777-9s (funnily enough, First and Business Class on the B777-9 will not offer OLED screens).
 Premium Economy Class screen 
 As for Economy Class, all we have is this shot of the new amenity kit with a slightly curved tray table in the background.
 Singapore Airlines new Economy Class seat 
 Oh, and a render of the 13-inch 4K screen, again with OLED on selected B777-9s.
 Economy Class screen 
 We will be seeing the new Premium Economy and Economy Class seats for the B777-9 today, so stay tuned for that.
 11.25 a.m
 What we know about the new Business Class
 On to Business Class, where we know substantially more, thanks to an expanded render that was published in the 2024/25 annual report.  This shows a suite with an external sliding privacy door , in a 1-2-1 staggered configuration with all forward-facing seats. 
 New Business Class render 
 Single seats alternate between being closer to the window and closer to the aisle. Window-aligned seats offer better privacy, as the console forms a barrier between the passenger and the aisle. Aisle-aligned seats are easier to get in and out of, with the loss of some privacy.
 For the seats in the middle, SIA has likely gone with a mix of “honeymoon” and “divorce” seats, which alternate between being pushed together or separated by the side console. 
 How do we know this? In the video featuring the new dining options, you can just about spot the outline of a sliding privacy partition on the right-hand side, which suggests that this lady is seated in one of the honeymoon seats.
 As for the bed, we know that the new Business Class seat will recline directly into a flat bed, with no flipping required. The manual flip-over mechanism will probably go down as one of the strangest innovations in seating history, and it’s telling that no other major carrier bar Air New Zealand and Virgin Atlantic ever adopted it.
 More importantly, a recline-to-flat design can be adjusted immediately after take-off, without having to wait until the seat belt sign goes off to stand up and flip the seat over. This allows passengers to fall asleep faster, which can be invaluable on those neither-here-nor-there redeye services.
 A staggered configuration also means that passengers will sleep parallel to the aisle and not at an angle, as is the case for SIA’s 2013 and 2017 Business Class seats. But if you needed further confirmation, there’s a brief glimpse of the bed in a shot where the new Business Class pyjamas are being placed. You can see the sleeping surface is clearly parallel to the door and hence the aisle.
 New Business Class seat in bed mode 
 Other shots include a closeup of the tray table, which doesn’t reveal much beyond a literature pocket in the background with the safety card visible. There’s also a look at the grey side console, which has a visible “lip” to stop loose items from sliding off. The new BYREDO amenity kit is placed here, which blocks off further details.
 New Business Class seat tray table New Business Class seat side console 
 Business Class seats will offer a 22-inch 4K OLED screen, USB-C and wireless charging, together with Bluetooth audio connectivity. 
 New Business Class seat inflight entertainment screen 
 11.20 a.m
 What we know about the new First Class
 We know that the new First Class seat will have three windows and French doors, electrically-operated blinds, and an ottoman for companion dining. This marks a return of the concept, which has been missing ever since the retirement of the first-generation Suites during the pandemic.
 New First Class render New First Class French doors 
 We’ve also seen shots of the suite’s interior, including a massive 32″ 4K OLED screen, a luxuriously-dressed bed, a vanity mirror, and backlit seat buttons set against wood grain panelling. Passengers will also enjoy — for the first time — B&O wireless headphones (SIA previously announced that wireless headphones would be introduced in Suites in 2018, but as far as I know, that never happened).
 New First Class entertainment screen New First Class bed New First Class storage nook and vanity mirror New First Class seat controls New First Class seat B&O wireless headphones 
 That’s all we have for now, but if you really want to get the tin foil hat on, a leaked patent filing that surfaced in late 2024 showed what appears to be the schematics of SIA’s First Class seat. 
 The document shows six First Class suites, with four window seats and two centre seats. Two centre seats can be combined into a double suite, with a privacy partition that fully retracts sideways (not downwards). Each suite has a separate seat and bed, though the seat must be stowed to make way for the bed — similar to the first generation Suites. 
 There’s an ottoman with a secondary seatbelt for couple dining, and suites will be fully enclosed, with curved walls to create additional space in the compartments. 
 It’s important to remember that the patent filing relates to the proposed layout for the Boeing 777-9, and not the four-seat First Class cabin on the Airbus A350-900ULR. However, the two will likely have very similar DNA, so the rest of the features should be largely identical.
 11.15 a.m
 What do we know so far? (continued)
 But what about the new seats?
 Singapore Airlines has been on an information lockdown where the new cabin products are concerned, no doubt wanting to avoid a repeat of 2017, where pictures of the new Suites leaked a few days before the official unveiling. 
 I understand that the new seats have only been seen by a very select group of people within the organisation. In fact, I was at a PPS event a few weeks ago, and spoke to someone on the SIA Events team who was responsible for organising today’s event. She said that even she was in the dark about the new seats.
 That said, SIA has released several videos, showcasing its new inflight menus, serviceware, amenities and KrisWorld system. Inside are some subtle glimpses of the new seats, which, when combined the teaser renders previously released, give us some clue as to what we can expect to see. I’ve written more about that here. 
 The funniest thing is: this fourth video probably cost the most to produce, yet tells you the least. 
 And that last scene where everyone wakes up and it turns out they were on an airplane? BAM INCEPTION OUT OF NOWHERE. 
 11.10 a.m
 What do we know so far?
 Over the past few weeks, Singapore Airlines has been performing what one executive referred to as the equivalent of a “marketing striptease”, by drip-feeding announcements about its new travel experience.
 However, these have been predominantly focused on the soft product:
 More than 100 new and refreshed dishes across all cabins, plus new Christofle serviceware in Suites, First and Business Class
 New First Class menu items New Business Class menu items New Premium Economy Class menu items New Economy Class menu items 
 New amenity kits by Sisley and BYREDO, and sleeper suits for Business Class passengers for the first time
 Suites & First Class Women’s SISLEY Amenity Kit Suites & First Class Men’s SISLEY Amenity Kit Suites & First Class sleeper suit Business Class BYREDO Amenity Kit Business Class Sleeper Suit 
 A refreshed First Class ground experience at Changi Airport, with a personal concierge, buggy service, priority security screening, and enhanced lounge dining
 The First Class SilverKris Lounge now offers table service 
 A redesigned KrisWorld with spatial audio and more than 2,500 entertainment options, paired with Starlink low-earth orbit satellite connectivity 
 These are all welcome improvements, but it’s really just the foreplay before the main event — the new seats.
 11.03 a.m
 More things people are hoping to see today
 Many of you are sharing more things you hope to see from SIA today.
 “A smart TV style entertainment system that lets you sign in to YouTube or Netflix from your own account”, says Michelle in Singapore. That’s an interesting idea, though I suspect if it were possible, some airline would be offering it already. I’m guessing there are licensing issues.
 “Headphone free stereo integrated into headrest wings, like JAL — but hopefully not like our MRTs with uncle/aunties watching TikToks” , says Chris, direct from the MRT First cabin. Hey, it’s easier to police noise pollution when you can threaten to eject anyone out the emergency exit.
 “First Class showers on the B777X”, says Max. The only way you can be legally naked at 35,000 feet (not Quentin Tarantino feet).
 “Dine on demand, adjustable pillow inserts, lockers for personal belongings, screen mirroring for personal devices, anti glare adaptive zonal personal reading light, high speed charging”, says Shaun, who has clearly done his research.
 10.52 a.m
 Too little, too late?
 So did SIA leave it too late? I know many people think so.
 When it became apparent that the Boeing 777X issues would not be resolved anytime soon, other carriers like Cathay Pacific and Lufthansa made the call to install their new seats on different aircraft instead.
 SIA decided to wait, and passed on several opportunities to do so (like when the ULRs went for heavy maintenance in May 2024). As a result, it’s still flying 2013-era seats on routes where its rivals have surged far ahead.
 Today’s event will tell us whether the airline can leapfrog them again, or whether it’s just playing catching up.
 💬 Have Your Say 
 With all the delays to its new cabin products, how would you rate SIA against its competitors now? 
 ➡️Share your thoughts! 
 10.40 a.m
 What are these seats replacing?
 But if you want to find the seats that today’s next-generation cabin products are directly replacing, you’ll have to go back even further to 9 July 2013.  
 That’s when Singapore Airlines unveiled its 2013 First and Business Class seats, which made their debut on a factory-fitted B777-300ER to London in September 2013.
 MileLion reader Alan has dug this one out from the archives.
 Click to enlarge 
 Here are some photos of that event — held at the CIP Terminal — courtesy of SIA’s Facebook page. 
 SIA 2013 launch event — new First Class | Photo: SIA SIA 2013 launch event — new First Class | Photo: SIA SIA 2013 launch event — new Business Class | Photo: SIA SIA 2013 launch event — new Business Class | Photo: SIA SIA 2013 launch event — new Economy Class | Photo: SIA 
 From the CIP Terminal to Suntec City to Marina Bay Sands. Talk about going places!
 These are the seats that most SIA long-haul passengers are still flying today. 
 10.32 a.m
 SIA’s last major product launch
 So, when was SIA’s last major product launch?
 Well, in November 2021, the airline launched its narrowbody cabin products for the B737-8 MAX, and in March 2018, the regional Business Class for the B787-10 (and later, A350-900MH). But these were smaller, relatively low-key events (especially the B737-8, because of COVID-era restrictions).
 SIA 2021 Regional Business Class unveiling 
 For the last all-hands event, you’d have to go back to 2 November 2017, when SIA unveiled its new cabin products for the Airbus A380 at Suntec City Convention Centre.
 The theme was “Space Made Personal” , and indeed it was, with the unveiling of the new Suites Class, which offered guests a private room in the sky. Sure, it wasn’t perfect, but that was probably the last SIA seat released that made you go “wow”.
 SIA 2017 launch event — new Suites | Photo: yflyer via SQTalk 
 The new Business Class seats didn’t offer doors (remember, this was the year Qatar Airways debuted the Qsuite), but they marked an epoch in their own way, since it was the first time that SIA abandoned the flip-over seat mechanism in favour of a recline-to-flat design. It was also significantly more couple-friendly, with a privacy divider that could be fully lowered, and no view-obstructing wings at eye-level. 
 Strangely, despite the considerable sum that must have gone into developing these, they were only ever installed on 12 A380s. 
 SIA 2017 launch event — new Business Class | Photo: yflyer via SQTalk 
 Premium Economy wasn’t a new product as such — the seat had been launched two years earlier in August 2015 on the A380-800. 
 But Economy got a new slimline seat from Recaro, which has since found its way onto selected A350-900LHs and B787-10s as well. 
 SIA 2017 launch event — new Economy Class | Photo: yflyer via SQTalk 
 At the event, SIA also showcased its new Lalique-branded bedding, toiletries, glassware and China for Suites, Penhaligon’s toiletries in Business Class, and new menu items.
 10.23 a.m
 What do you hope to see from SIA today?
 Some initial thoughts coming in of what you guys hope to see from SIA’s latest and greatest today.
 “Massage function and zero G seat setting for new First Class”, says Fat Jo, currently serving our country in reservist where massages can be dangerous things.
 “More privacy in Business Class, more integration with smartphones and headphones, wireless chargers and Bluetooth connectivity” , says Daryl Tan in Singapore, echoing a lot of the complaints about SIA’s current 2013J seat.
 “Caviar in Business Class”, says Daniel in Singapore, referring to a leaked tender in August 2025 showing the airline soliciting bids for “supply of farmed caviar for Business Class” — something we’ve heard nothing about since.  
 “A true “wow” moment that sets a new benchmark like the original Suites did, like a revolutionary concept or a feature that no one saw coming, something the competition spends the next decade trying to emulate”, says Kelvin. You and me both, sir.
 10.15 a.m
 You ask, I test
 I’ve come prepared today. Inside my bag is a measuring tape, HDMI cable, USB-C cable with wattage indicator, spare phone, and all manner of items to poke and pry and prod these new seats in ways that will challenge the boundaries of good taste.
 Can you reach your shoes when the seat is in bed mode? Can you access the seat controls when reclined? Do cables run across your sleeping area? Do the power outlets have sufficient clearance? How’s the socket grip? How big is the foot cubby? Is the tray table sturdy enough for robust typing? Are there gaps in the seat where small items could fall in?
 But I’m sure there are plenty of things you want to know that I haven’t even thought about. 
 So here’s where I need your help. Send in the things you’d like me to test, and once the hands-on portion begins, I’ll try to get some answers. Also, I’ll have an opportunity to chat with the people behind the seats, so share your questions and I’ll see what I can find out.
 Submit your questions here. 
 10.05 a.m
 How to participate
 My precious 
 For years, The MileLioness has been nagging me to declutter my amenity kit and sleeper suit collection. 
 “Sure I will,” I said. “As soon as the new SIA cabin products launch!”
 Then I guffawed and walked away, but joke’s on me, because that day has finally come. Now I have to clear:
 20x Le Labo Business Class amenity kits
 11x Penhaligon’s Business Class amenity kits
 2x Lalique First Class amenity kits
 7x Lalique First Class sleeper suits
 So let’s have some fun with this. I’m going to share some ways you can participate in today’s live blog, and if your contribution is featured, I’ll mail you one of these at random, while stocks last (sorry, Singapore addresses only please). 
 Hey, with SIA unveiling new SISLEY and BYREDO amenity kits , these will be collector’s items soon!
 Before someone asks, all of these are unopened and unused — though for a nominal fee, I will consider perfuming myself and rolling around a few times in the sleeper suits and/or performing Squat Cobbler. The reason why some are wrapped in plastic and others aren’t is because SIA did away with the packaging a few years back, as part of their go-green initiatives.
 You can share your thoughts via this Google Form. Alternatively, you can join our Telegram community (please submit via Google Form if you want to take part in the giveaway though), which I’m sure will be extra lively today.
 Let’s kick this off with a nice, easy one.
 💬 Have Your Say 
 What are you hoping to see from Singapore Airlines today? 
 ➡️Share your thoughts! 
 There will be a separate link for any questions you want to ask about the new seats or cabin experience, which I’ll share shortly.
 9.53 a.m
 Today’s schedule
 Here’s a rundown of the order of battle for today.
 Today’s event is called “The New Singapore Airlines Travel Experience” (yes, a catchier name like “thanks, Boeing” would have been better).
 The event will be held at the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre — ticketed visitors only, in case you were hoping to gatecrash — and will show off not just the new seats, but all aspects of SIA’s cabin enhancements including new dishes, new amenity kits, new sleeper suits and more.
 The event will commence at 1.15 p.m, with opening remarks by SIA CEO Goh Choon Phong.
 At 1.30 p.m , the media embargo will lift, and I’ll be able to share with you the full details of SIA’s new cabin products.
 From then until the event concludes at 5.30 p.m,  the media will have their first hands-on time with the next-generation cabin products, the enhanced KrisWorld inflight entertainment system, refreshed F&B offerings, new amenity kits and soft furnishings.
 I’m going to do my best to keep this blog regularly updated, though there may be a bit of a slowdown in the afternoon as I do the hands-on. 
 It’s my first time running a live blog, so go easy on me. Not exactly the kind of thing you picture yourself doing for a living when you graduate with an accounting degree…
 9.45 a.m
 Here we go!
 Good morning everyone, and welcome to what is going to be an absolutely massive day for Singapore Airlines.
 This is it. D-Day. Disclosure Day. The day the airline finally unveils its highly anticipated — and long delayed — next generation seats and new cabin experience at a glitzy event at Marina Bay Sands.
 In a way, it’s an apt choice of venue, because the stakes could not be higher. At the risk of sounding dramatic, believe me when I say this is do-or-die time  for our national carrier. 
 Remember, if everything had gone according to plan, these seats and interiors would have been flying for half a decade now. They were originally supposed to arrive in 2021, on the Boeing 777-9.
 SilverKris Magazine, April 2020. The number of aircraft on order has since increased to 31 
 No prizes for guessing how that turned out, with COVID-19 and the endless dysfunction at Boeing causing the timeline to slip repeatedly for the largest passenger aircraft ever built since the Airbus A380. 
 Singapore Airlines waited, and waited, and waited — perhaps longer than it should have — before finally biting the bullet and announcing in November 2024 that it would introduce the new First and Business Class on retrofitted Airbus A350-900s instead. 
 But even Plan B ran into a snag. The targeted Q2 2026 introduction was beset by supply chain and certification issues, which pushed the introduction into Q1 2027.  
 In the meantime, rivals such as ANA, British Airways, Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Korean Air,   Qatar Airways and STARLUX are already flying impressive new Business Class suites with privacy doors. Even Malaysia Airlines — no disrespect — got doors in Business Class before SIA! Entire product life-cycles have been completed within the lifespan of SIA’s 2013 Business Class seat. United introduced Polaris 1.0 in 2016; Polaris 2.0 began flying in April 2026.
 All this to say: today’s event has been a long time coming. 
 I’m incredibly excited for the big reveal, and I know many of you are too. So join me as I bring you all the latest from SIA’s launch event, complete with blow-by-blow updates, photos and videos, and irreverent commentary.
 Bookmark this page and refresh it for the latest updates. I’ll also be sharing how you can participate in this live blog, with giveaways and internet points up for grabs.
 Buckle up, because it’s going to be an eventful day!
